reasoning: Plan A is significantly better suited for an athlete aiming to become a faster trail runner. It incorporates targeted hill work, tempo runs, and a dedicated strength session – all crucial for improving power, efficiency, and the ability to maintain speed on varied terrain. Plan B, conversely, focuses almost exclusively on low-intensity aerobic running, which, while beneficial for building a base, won't directly translate to faster trail times. Plan A’s inclusion of structured speed work and strength training addresses the specific demands of trail running, making it a more effective plan for achieving the stated goal.
